newsitem.title: CANADA: Fonorola denies AT&T Canada deal report.
newsitem.headline: Fonorola denies AT&T Canada deal report.

text.p: Fonorola Inc is not in talks with AT&T Long Distance Services Co on a possible equity tie-up, the company's president and chief executive Jan Peeters said on Monday.
"We're not talking to AT&T. There are no conversations going on with AT&T at all," Peeters said in a telephone interview.
A report in the Globe and Mail newspaper quoted sources as saying that a committee of both companies has finished due diligence and a deal could be unveiled as early as the end of next week.
But Peeters said there is no truth to these reports.
Another source cited in the article said Peeters had been spotted in the AT&T Canada Long Distance executive offices.
"I have never been on the executive floor of AT&T since (former Unitel Communications Inc chairman and chief executive) George Harvey stepped down," Peeters said.

Peeters said the only possible justification for the rumors may be that Fonorola's partner in a 48-strand Edmonton-Toronto fibre-optic network, construction company Ledcor Industries Ltd, may be talking to interested parties about selling its portion of the network.

"In all likelihood, Ledcor has been talking to AT&T and for that matter, Sprint Canada and Rogers (Communications Inc ) and anybody else that would be a logical buyer of (fibre-optic) strands in Canada," Peeters said.
AT&T Canada Long Distance, Unitel's corporate successor, is owned by AT&T Corp unit AT&T Canada as well as three Canadian banks.
"It's speculation as far as we are concerned," said AT&T Canada Long Distance spokeswoman Carleen Carroll.
AT&T Canada spokesman Murray Luening said he could not comment on the affairs of AT&T Canada Long Distance.
A solid climb in Fonorola's share price prompted the company to issue a release earlier this month saying there were no corporate developments to account for this.

Peeters attributed the price rise to good sales and cash flow growth, to the small public float which keeps Fonorola shares in scant supply and to the high demand by institutional investors for shares sold recently by Telesystem National.

"By the time the dust settled between the buyers and sellers, that transaction came in at considerably above the stock price at the beginning of the year -- and sort of set a new trend for the stock price," Peeters said.
-- Sarah Edmonds, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100, E-mail sarah.edmonds@reuters.com
